history.summary: Integrated development sitting atop Compass One mall with direct access to Sengkang MRT/LRT and bus interchange — unbeatable convenience at a low $1.8M quantum for a large 1,324 sqft 3BR. PSF 1360 is just ~1% above the URA median and 7.7%/yr resale CAGR is the strongest of the Serangoon/Sengkang names. Aging 2003 build and common-area upkeep gripes keep it a Buy rather than Strong Buy.
history.rating_rationale: The integrated-development premium is the thesis: directly above Compass One, with Sengkang MRT (NEL), LRT and bus interchange below — the kind of doorstep connectivity that holds resale value. 7.7%/yr resale CAGR (highest among the non-Punggol D19 names) on 80 txns, a $1.8M quantum in the deep buyer band, and a large 1,324 sqft layout all support the case. PSF 1360 is essentially at-median (URA 1344), so not a discount but fair for the location. Offsets: 2003 build (23 years), and reviews flag aging common-area upkeep (smell/pests at the L1 MRT entrance). The convenience moat outweighs the age drag.

history.summary: Aging (2002) Sengkang MRT-linked leasehold priced at the top of its own recent range, not below it — asking $1,430 psf vs recent comparable transactions of $1,379-$1,409; the high trailing CAGR carries no forward weight.
history.rating_rationale: The value signal is weak/absent. Recent deals (Nov-2025 to Jan-2026) printed $1,379-$1,409 psf, and the current PSF range tops out near $1,496; the asking $1,430 psf is at the upper end of recent transactions, not a discount. The algo's age-adj premium is only -1.0% (essentially fairly priced), and the +9.3% vs-cohort premium rests on just 3 cohort txns, so there's no robust cheapness to lead with. The headline 7.65% trailing CAGR (and +20% 2023-26 PSF) is exactly the trailing momentum the v3.4 backtest shows has ~0 forward power — story only. Physically it's a 24-year-old 99yr-from-2000 leasehold (~74 years left), described as dated with outdated gym/dark lift lobbies, pest issues, and pneumatic-waste noise. The one genuine merit is direct integration with Sengkang MRT and Compass One mall (D19 OCR, a favourable forward region), which keeps it from an Avoid but does not justify paying near the top of the range.

history.summary: A 1,507 sqft 3BR (2 baths) at Compass Heights — a 2002/03 99-LH integrated development sitting directly on Sengkang MRT/LRT and Compass One mall — asking $1.75M / $1,161 psf. The algo's 834 score rests on a −12.6% discount to the project median and −20.8% to the age-adjusted D19 size band, but both benchmarks are contaminated by size mix: Compass Heights' PSF falls off a cliff above ~1,550 sqft, and the project's own large-unit prints, time-adjusted, sit at ~$1,100–$1,270 psf. Against its true comp set the ask is fairly priced, not cheap — leaving an outstanding location with a thin 3.1% yield, a 73-year lease and no verified value cushion.
history.rating_rationale: The discount does not survive verification. URA prints for this project (80 txns, 2021–May-26), time-adjusted to 2026 on the project's own median-PSF index, split by size: 1,230–1,340 sqft → ~$1,376 psf (n=36), 1,550 sqft → ~$1,374 psf (n=6), but 1,600–1,800 sqft → ~$1,201 psf (n=7, every single one floor 01–05), and the one genuine 1,507 sqft print (Jan-23, fl 01–05, $929 psf) adjusts to ~$1,117. The ask of $1,161 psf is therefore ~15% below the nearest-size 1,550 prints but roughly AT — even ~4% above — what this project's own large low-floor units actually fetch. The paired evidence is direct: Jan-23 1,507 sqft @ $929 vs May-23 1,550 sqft @ $1,077, same floor band, four months apart — a 14% gap between the two layouts that has never closed. The listing's 2 bathrooms on 1,507 sqft (753 sqft/bath, vs 416–441 for the 1,249/1,324 sqft 3-bath stock asking the same $1.78–1.80M quantum) is the signature of that cheaper tier. I could not confirm the unit's floor — PropertyGuru is Cloudflare-blocked and there is no stack profile — and floor is the swing factor (Dec-25 1,550 fl 01–05 printed $1,274 vs Apr-26 fl 06–10 at $1,361). On a high floor there could be a real ~10% cushion; on the low floor the size cluster implies, there is none. Two agents listing the identical unit at the same price five days apart, $359k under the Apr-26 1,550 sqft print, reads as a lesser product or a bait ask rather than a mispricing a rational seller would leave on the table. Everything else is solid but not compelling: genuinely elite connectivity (56m to Sengkang NE16 + LRT + bus interchange + mall below), three primary schools inside 562m, 536 units and 50+ deals a year, OCR/D19 (the favoured region under current priors). Against that: 3.09% gross / 1.78% net yield, 73 years of lease left (66 at exit), and a size band that has traded twice in five years while the 1,230–1,340 band traded 36 times — project liquidity is deep, this unit type's is not. Mixed signals that balance out: Neutral.
red_flags: Headline discount is a size-mix artifact — −12.6% vs project median and −20.8% vs the age-adjusted D19 1,400–1,800 band are measured against benchmarks dominated by 667–1,340 sqft stock; vs the project's own large-unit prints the ask is at or above fair (psf_cohort_txns = 4, thin)

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Adequate but unexciting. realsmart shows 33 rental contracts in the past month at ~$4.00 psf avg and a median rent of $3,350 (the recent contract list is 1BR-heavy); a 1,300–1,400 sqft 3BR let at $4,450/mo on 1 Jun 2026. The DB's $4,500/mo assumption for this 1,507 sqft unit (rent_source ura_project_bed, confidence 0.95) is therefore realistic to marginally generous — large units do not command proportionally more rent, so the extra 180 sqft over a 1,324 sqft 3BR earns almost nothing. That gives 3.09% gross / 1.78% net, below the 3.6% realsmart estimates for the project as a whole (which is pulled up by the small units). Tenant demand itself is strong and reliable — MRT-on-the-doorstep, mall below, Punggol Digital District employment nearby — but the tenant pool for a $4,500 3BR in Sengkang is thinner than for the 1BR/2BR stock. Treat the yield as carry only; the backtest shows high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth, and this is the low-yield end of the same trade-off.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 7.65%/yr URA figure is trailing and should not be underwritten. It measures 2021 ($893 psf project median) to 2026 ($1,361) — a +52% run off a COVID-era trough — and the project's size mix shifts year to year, so part of it is composition rather than price. Under current priors trailing CAGR carries ~zero marginal forward power. I would underwrite closer to the OCR regional baseline of ~3.5–4%/yr, less a modest drag for a lease running 73 → 66 years over the hold, i.e. ~3%/yr net of decay. The ROI table's 7.2% annualized is the data rate compounded and should be read as an upper bound, not a plan. I have left appreciation_rate_override_pct null: there is no dated project-specific catalyst to justify substituting my own number, and the resale-to-resale evidence supports the level critique above rather than a specific alternative rate. Realsmart's backward-looking record is respectable but not exceptional — REALSCORE 3.4/5, 85.9% of 617 matched resale pairs profitable, $156.9M total profits, 4.3% average annualized profit over the past year on a 7.9-year average hold. Read as downside evidence: owners here have usually done fine, but 14% did not, which is a genuine tail on a deep sample and argues against paying up for the story.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No stack profile exists for Compass Heights (status: not_researched) and the listing carries no floor, stack or facing — PropertyGuru is Cloudflare-blocked so I could not recover them. What the URA prints do reveal is a strong floor/size coupling: every one of the seven 1,600–1,800 sqft prints since 2021 is floor 01–05, as is the single 1,507 sqft print and the 1,410 sqft print, while the 1,550 sqft layout trades across 01–05, 06–10 and 11–15 at $1,274 / $1,329–1,361 / $1,342 psf respectively. The large layouts in this project appear concentrated on low floors — which, in a development built over a mall and a bus interchange, is exactly where footfall and noise are worst. Combined with 2 baths on 1,507 sqft, the most probable read is a low-floor unit of the cheaper large-format tier. Running /research-development on Compass Heights would resolve this and is the single highest-value next step: if this unit is in fact on floor 8+, the ~10% cushion becomes credible and the rating moves up.
